# Review of the supplied proposals

The department table is a catalog of suggested skills, grouped into repeatable processes, connected-tool work, and conventions. It contains no installed skill implementation, authenticated account connection, execution proof, or permissions policy. Useful candidates for HezTech are design-doc-to-plan, ops-playbook-writer, exec-decision-brief, and policy-qa-from-knowledgebase. Connected-tool skills require their real account adapter and verified output; prose alone must never mark them operational.

The supplied PowerShell writes orbit-gravity-brain.html beside the packaged application. Its computed uiPath is unused; it does not modify the React route or app.asar. Its navigation, search, and conversation button have no handlers. It generates exactly 52 synthetic nodes and arbitrary hub links, hardcodes CPU/RAM, loads unpinned CDN scripts (3d-force-graph twice), and its rotation slider resets the camera rather than rotating by the selected value. Consequently its success message does not prove integration. It was reviewed as text, not executed.

The implemented route keeps the current memory/conversation graph builder and tag-only edge semantics. It uses locally bundled 3d-force-graph 1.80.1, MIT, https://github.com/vasturiano/3d-force-graph. It provides WebGL orbit/zoom/select, actual-data search, fit view, a keyboard-accessible node list, literal-text tooltips, responsive sizing, and page-unmount cleanup. It does not invent semantic relationships, install any department skill, or change credentials/social publishing/CapCut. GPU/WebGL acceleration helps rendering; no AI model GPU is required by the graph itself. If WebGL is unavailable, the real node list and details remain usable.

Validation on 2026-10-31: TypeScript/Vite build and Electron packaging passed. Four knowledge test files passed (six tests), covering graph construction, navigation, real-data selection, literal-text labels, lifecycle cleanup, and unavailable-WebGL feedback. The actual packaged desktop passed its offline knowledge acceptance: 53 actual records/tags, real WebGL canvas, keyboard selection, search, route teardown/remount, no renderer exceptions, no renderer Node access, and no secret exposure through configuration IPC. Evidence: stack/evidence/heztech-2.0.3/acceptance-knowledge-3d.json and 07-knowledge-3d-after.png. Before image: knowledge-3d-before.png. This check does not claim that chat memory, Live voice, social dispatch, or CapCut edits are complete.

The build reports a 1.42 MB minified, dynamically loaded Three.js graph bundle (382 KB gzip), plus its development source map. It is not fetched from a CDN at runtime. Existing unrelated Vite chunk-size, localStorage experimental, and React Router future-flag warnings remain visible.
